newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Right's Aleman takes early lead in Nicaragua vote.
newsitem.headline: Right's Aleman takes early lead in Nicaragua vote.

text.p: First official results from Nicaragua's presidential election put right-winger Arnoldo Aleman ahead of his main challenger, Sandinista revolutionary leader Daniel Ortega, local election authorities said early on Monday.
With 2.58 percent of the votes counted, the preliminary official results gave Aleman 19,120 votes against 15,265 for Ortega.
The results showed Aleman of the Liberal Alliance held a strong advantage with 49.83 percent of the vote compared with Ortega's 40 percent, the Supreme Election Council said.

A victory above 45 percent would mean Aleman would win the presidency without having to face a second-round showdown against Ortega's Sandinista National Liberation Front, which ruled Nicaragua from 1979 to 1990.
The two front-runners were far ahead of the other 21 presidential candidates on the ballot, who gained just a small portion of the vote.

The result was also in line with private "quick count" surveys broadcast unofficially by local television minutes prior to the result announcement, despite a ban by electoral authorities. Aleman's supporters were already celebrating victory early on Monday.
